themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Claims product leadership across four families: solutions in Manual Transmission, state-of-the-art 4WD systems, "India's largest EV Transmission manufacturer" and "Pioneer in Automatic Transmission in India".
- States it is "the only supplier in India to have inhouse capability to conceive, design, develop, manufacture and supply grounds up EV transmission", tooled up and ready for series production from 10kW to 150kW.
- Positions itself as a trusted partner for global and leading OEMs, citing M&M (long-term strategic relationship), Tata (long-term EV ecosystem partnership), Force Motors (diversification), BorgWarner ("Most Transformational Collaboration"), Magna and Toyota Tsusho (entry into the Japanese ecosystem).
- Marquee customer relationships are shown as long-dated — 50+ years, 50+ years, 30+ years and multiple 10+ year relationships spanning EV transmission, transfer cases, synchronisers, MT components, ALH and NexTrac.
- Vision stated as "To be recognized as a world-class Indian brand in automotive drivetrain components and systems" and to "Emerge as one of the fastest growing drivetrain solution companies in the world".

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Indonesia order] Secured an exclusive order as sole supplier from a key OEM customer for 4x4 transfer cases for the Indonesian Pik-Up program, with production expected from CY26; the Indonesia 4x4 ramp-up is named as the primary growth driver, with incremental volumes expected through the remaining quarters of FY27.
- [Export approvals] Received final production approval on all export parts with additional revenue potential of ~Rs. 10 to 12 crores per month; FY27 component exports are targeted at ~Rs. 80 crore.
- [Export trajectory] Exports revenue of Rs. 13.55 Cr (FY23), Rs. 3.42 Cr (FY24), Rs. 10.80 Cr (FY25) and Rs. 66.90 Cr (FY26), with the FY26 exports share shown at 18% of total revenue; geographic mix in the latest quarter shown as 84% Domestic / 16% Exports.
- [Partnership channel] Exclusive distribution agreement with Toyota Tsusho for Divgi-TTS products to Japanese companies worldwide, opening Japan, South Korea, Thailand, Indonesia and China; new AWD and PTU programmes cited as further diversification avenues.
- [Ownership history] Journey slide records the BorgWarner JV, BorgWarner's exit via buy-out of shares, investments by NRJN Family Trust and Oman India Joint Investment Fund II, and the 2020 amalgamation into Divgi TorqTransfer Systems.
